blocks.text: Numbers 24 contains 25 verses. It opens with: And when Balaam saw that it pleased Jehovah to bless Israel, he went not, as at the other times, to meet with enchantments, but he set his face toward the wilderness. It concludes with: And Balaam rose up, and went and returned to his place; and Balak also went his way. Supplied contextual evidence for this passage adds: In Numbers 22-24, Balak summons Balaam to curse Israel, but Balaam repeatedly delivers blessings under divine constraint. The Deir Alla inscription attests a later nonbiblical tradition about Balaam son of Beor, but it does not independently verify the speeches or events narrated in Numbers 22-24.
